item.title: Clocks springing forward this weekend, B.C. adopts year-round daylight time
item.description: OTTAWA — Clocks are set to spring forward on Sunday as most of Canada moves to daylight time until the fall. Daylight time begins at 2 a.m. on Sunday, March 8, when clocks move forward one hour, until November 1, when they’ll be turned back an hour to rejoin standard time. Except in British Columbia, […]

item.title: Deadline extended for applications to design sculpture outside new Dawson Creek hospital
item.description: The deadline for expression of interests in designing a sculpture outside the new Dawson Creek and District Hospital has been extended from March 6th to March 27th. Artists who wish to apply must submit a resume and portfolio of past work.

item.title: Northern Lights College finds new location for Tumbler Ridge campus after tragedy
item.description: Northern Lights College (NLC) has found a new location for its Tumbler Ridge campus, after a mass shooting at its former home in the Tumbler Ridge Secondary School building.

item.title: Fifth person charged for 2022 double homicide in Penticton: RCMP
item.description: PENTICTON — The RCMP say a 36-year-old man has been charged with two counts of first-degree murder in connection with a 2022 double homicide in Penticton, B.C. Police say the BC Prosecution Service has approved two counts of first-degree murder against Yves “Oliver” Grenier in connection with the deaths of Douglas Barker and Alannah Brown. […]

item.title: B.C. government to keep antlers and hide after decision overturned in guided hunt case
item.description: Zachary McDermott was found guilty of killing a mountain sheep out of season on a guided hunt. B.C. is keeping the antlers and hide after an appeal which overturned a previous decision.

item.title: Strong winds cause power outages across B.C. overnight
item.description: BC Hydro has reported nearly 70 power outages overnight on March 7th and 8th across B.C. amidst a yellow wind warning.

item.title: Fort St. John talks potential west coast pipeline with Alberta minister
item.description: Fort St. John councillors joined the mayor, Lilia Hansen, to meet Alberta minister of Indigenous relations Rajan Sawhney to discuss the West Coast Oil Pipeline project.
